instructions:
# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

items.t: The Arogyamitra desk at any MJPJAY network (empanelled) hospital in Maharashtra, government or private; it is usually near the main reception. Take the original ration card (or the domicile certificate) and the patient's Aadhaar card. The list of network hospitals is on jeevandayee.gov.in and is also given on the toll-free number 155388. The Ayushman card itself can be made beforehand at a CSC (Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra), through the ASHA worker, or at the same hospital desk.
The 12-digit number printed on the ration card. The Arogyamitra uses it to find your whole family in the scheme list.
Ration card colour
Orange
Yellow, orange, white, AAY or Annapurna are all accepted. If you have no ration card, show the Maharashtra domicile certificate instead.
Patient's name (as on Aadhaar)
Vithabai Dnyandeo Shinde
Exactly as printed on the patient's Aadhaar card, so that the e-KYC matches.
Patient's Aadhaar number
The patient's own Aadhaar, not the head of family's. An OTP, fingerprint or face scan confirms it.
Mother
How the patient is related to the person named first on the ration card.
A number someone in the family keeps with them; messages about approval and discharge come here.
District / Taluka
Solapur / Pandharpur
Treatment needed
Gall bladder stone operation
The doctor writes this after examining the patient. The hospital then asks the scheme for approval of that package.
Admission type
Planned (not emergency)
In an emergency the hospital starts treatment at once and informs the scheme by phone or email; the papers can follow.

When a doctor says the patient needs an operation or admission, ask whether the hospital is an MJPJAY / Ayushman network hospital. If you are not sure, call 155388 or look up the hospital list on jeevandayee.gov.in.
Go to the Arogyamitra desk with the ration card and the patient's Aadhaar. The Arogyamitra registers the patient on the scheme portal and does the Aadhaar e-KYC by OTP, fingerprint or face scan.

The doctor examines the patient, and the hospital sends a pre-authorisation request online to the State Health Assurance Society with the reports. Approval usually comes within hours; in an emergency, treatment starts first.
Once approved, the listed treatment, operation, medicines, tests, bed and food are free. Do not pay cash or sign any paper promising to pay for a listed treatment.
At discharge you receive the discharge summary. The hospital's bill goes to the government, not to you.
If a hospital asks for money for a covered treatment, call 155388 or 1800-233-2200 before paying and tell them the hospital's name.
To make the next visit quicker, get the Ayushman card made for every family member at a CSC, through the ASHA worker or at the Arogyamitra desk.
155388 / 1800-233-2200 (MJPJAY toll-free call centre); 14555 (Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY)
Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana (Niradhar Pension)
Social Justice and Special Assistance Department, Government of Maharashtra (through the Tehsildar)

A monthly pension of Rs.1,500 for people under 65 who have no one to support them: persons with 40% or more disability, people with serious illnesses such as cancer, TB, HIV or leprosy, widows, divorced or abandoned women, orphan children and transgender persons, among others. Disabled beneficiaries get Rs.2,500 a month from October 2025. The money comes every month by DBT into an Aadhaar-linked bank account. You apply through the talathi or the tehsil office; the state has also opened online applications on the MahaDBT portal.
Rs.1,500 a month (Rs.2,500 for disabled beneficiaries)
Living in Maharashtra for at least 15 years; aged 18 to below 65 (orphan or disabled children under 18 get it through a guardian)
Family income up to Rs.21,000 a year, or up to Rs.50,000 a year if the applicant is disabled; or the family is on the BPL list

Belongs to a destitute group: disabled (40% or more, UDID card needed), serious illness, widow, divorced or abandoned woman, woman whose divorce is pending, unmarried woman of 35 or more with no support, orphan child, transgender person, or the family of a farmer who died by suicide
Not drawing a regular monthly benefit from any government, semi-government or local body
At 65 the beneficiary moves to the Shravanbal or the central old-age pension
Aadhaar card, and MGNREGA job card if you have one
Residence certificate from the gram panchayat or talathi, and the ration card
Age proof: birth certificate or school leaving certificate
Income certificate from the tehsildar, or BPL certificate
Proof of your category: UDID card, husband's death certificate, court divorce papers, orphan certificate, medical certificate of the illness, or transgender certificate
First page of an Aadhaar-linked bank passbook in your own name
Signed self-declaration with a passport-size photograph

The talathi (gram mahsul adhikari) of your village, or the Sanjay Gandhi Yojana branch of the tehsil office; in a city, the tehsil office of your area. The prescribed application is Form 3 of Annexure 1 (page 20) of the government resolution linked here, and the tehsil office and Setu or Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendras also keep blank forms. Hand in two copies of the form and of each certificate, carry the originals for checking, and ask for a dated acknowledgement.
To: Tehsildar, Taluka / District
Tehsildar, Taluka Paithan / District Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar
The tehsil where you live now.
Applicant's full name
Mangal Rajendra Waghmare
As on Aadhaar, with husband's or father's name in the middle.
At post Pachod, Tal. Paithan
Your present address, with village or ward.
You must be at least 18 and below 65.
Residence in Maharashtra
Since birth (48 years)
At least 15 years is required. The residence certificate is the proof.
Attach a copy. The pension is paid only to an account linked with this Aadhaar.
Number of family members
Everyone living and eating together in the household.
Total yearly family income from all sources
Add up all earnings, including support from grown sons. It must be Rs.21,000 or less (Rs.50,000 if you are disabled), as shown on the income certificate.
Category of destitute
Tick one: disabled, illness, destitute woman, widow, divorced, abandoned, orphan child, transgender, family of a farmer who died by suicide.
Aadhaar-linked bank account number and IFSC
An account in your own name. If it is not linked with Aadhaar the money does not arrive, so check at the bank first.

Collect the papers first: income certificate from the tehsildar (apply at a Setu or Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra), residence certificate, age proof and the proof of your category, such as the UDID card or husband's death certificate.
Get the form from the talathi, the tehsil office or a Setu kendra. Fill it in, sign or put your thumb impression in front of a witness, and attach the self-declaration with a photo.

Hand it to the talathi or at the tehsil's Sanjay Gandhi Yojana branch and take the acknowledgement. The talathi visits your home to check the papers and family income and uploads a photo of the visit.

The tehsildar checks the file and places it before the Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana committee, which meets every month. The lists of approved and rejected names are put on the notice board and read in the gram sabha.
Once approved, the pension starts from the month after the online process is complete and comes by DBT into your Aadhaar-linked account every month.

Keep your Aadhaar and bank linking in order, because payments that fail for Aadhaar or bank reasons are the beneficiary's responsibility. Give the life certificate each year when the tehsil asks; if the pension stopped, giving it in the same financial year restarts it.
If nothing happens for two or three months, go to the tehsil office with your acknowledgement and ask for the committee's decision.
Sanjay Gandhi Yojana branch of your tehsil office; 1800-120-8040 (Aaple Sarkar helpline)
Shravanbal Seva Rajya Nivruttivetan Yojana (Shravanbal Pension)

A monthly pension of Rs.1,500 for poor men and women aged 65 and above in Maharashtra. If the family is not on the BPL list but earns up to Rs.21,000 a year, the whole Rs.1,500 comes from the state (Group A). If the family is on the BPL list, the person gets the central Indira Gandhi old-age pension plus a Shravanbal top-up, again Rs.1,500 in all (Group B). Each eligible person is counted separately, so husband and wife can both get it, applying with one form each at the talathi or tehsil office; the money comes monthly by DBT.
Rs.1,500 a month per person
Aged 65 or above
Living in Maharashtra for at least 15 years
Group A: family not on the BPL list, with yearly family income up to Rs.21,000 (Rs.50,000 if the applicant is disabled)
Group B: family on the BPL list; gets the central old-age pension with the state top-up
Not drawing a regular monthly benefit or pension from any other government scheme
Age proof: birth certificate, school leaving certificate, or an age certificate from a government medical officer
Income certificate from the tehsildar, or BPL certificate or BPL list extract
UDID card, if the applicant is disabled

The talathi (gram mahsul adhikari) of your village, or the Sanjay Gandhi Yojana branch of the tehsil office, which also handles Shravanbal; in a city, the tehsil office of your area. The prescribed application is Form 3 of Annexure 1 (page 20) of the government resolution linked here, the same form as for the Niradhar pension, and the tehsil office and Setu or Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendras keep blank forms. Hand in two copies of the form and of each certificate, carry the originals, and ask for a dated acknowledgement.
Tehsildar, Taluka Sangamner / District Ahilyanagar
Kashinath Bhiku More
At post Ghargaon, Tal. Sangamner
You must have completed 65. If no paper shows your age, a government medical officer can give an age certificate.
Since birth (71 years)
At least 15 years is required.
Is the family below the poverty line?
Yes if the family is on the BPL list (Group B), No otherwise (Group A). The amount is the same either way.
Needed for Group A. Count all earnings, including help from sons. It must be Rs.21,000 or less, as shown on the income certificate.
Elderly
Tick elderly. Also mention a disability, if any, and attach the UDID card.
An account in your own name. Husband and wife should each give their own account.

Get the income certificate from the tehsildar through a Setu or Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra, or a BPL certificate if the family is on the BPL list, and keep the age proof and residence certificate ready.
Hand it to the talathi or at the tehsil's Sanjay Gandhi Yojana branch and take the acknowledgement. The talathi visits your home to check the papers and family income.

The tehsildar places the file before the Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana committee, which also decides Shravanbal cases every month. Approved names are put on the notice board and read in the gram sabha.
The pension starts from the month after approval is complete online and comes by DBT into your Aadhaar-linked account every month.
Give the life certificate each year when the tehsil asks. If the pension stopped, giving it in the same financial year restarts it.
Lek Ladki Yojana
Women and Child Development Department, Government of Maharashtra (ICDS Commissionerate)

Rs.1,01,000 in five instalments for a girl born on or after 1 April 2023 in a family with a yellow or orange ration card, paid at stages from her birth until she turns 18. It replaced the older Majhi Kanya Bhagyashree scheme. The parents apply through the anganwadi sevika, who fills in the form with them, uploads it to the scheme portal and gives a receipt. The money goes by DBT into a joint bank account of the girl and her mother.
Rs.1,01,000 in 5 parts: Rs.5,000 at birth, Rs.6,000 in Class 1, Rs.7,000 in Class 6, Rs.8,000 in Class 11, Rs.75,000 at 18
Girl born on or after 1 April 2023 to a family living in Maharashtra
The family holds a yellow or orange ration card and its yearly income is not more than Rs.1 lakh
Covers one or two daughters; if the family has a son and a daughter, the daughter gets it; twin girls at the second delivery both get it
For the 3rd instalment of the first child, or the 2nd instalment of the second child, the mother or father must give a family planning operation certificate
The bank account must be in Maharashtra; for the last Rs.75,000 the girl must be 18, unmarried and on the voter list
Girl's birth certificate (register the birth with the gram panchayat or municipality first)
Income certificate from the tehsildar showing yearly family income up to Rs.1 lakh
Attested copy of the yellow or orange ration card
Aadhaar of the parents, and of the girl (not needed for the first instalment)
First page of the passbook of the joint account of the girl and her mother
Proof of residence in Maharashtra
For later instalments: school bonafide certificate, family planning certificate, and at 18 her voter ID and a self-declaration that she is unmarried

The anganwadi sevika of your area, at the anganwadi centre. The application form is printed at the end of the scheme GR linked here (pages 9 to 12), and blank forms are also kept at every Child Development Project Officer (CDPO) office, the Zilla Parishad District Programme Officer's office and the District Women and Child Development Officer's office. Take the filled form with copies of the documents, carry the originals for checking, and ask the sevika for the signed receipt (pohoch pavti) at the bottom of the form. Apply the same way for each later instalment.
Applying for (first child / second child / twins)
First child
Tick the one that fits this girl. For twins born at the second delivery, tick twins.
Beneficiary's name
Swara Sachin Jadhav
The girl's name as written on her birth certificate.

Not yet made
The girl's Aadhaar is not needed for the first instalment. Get it made before the Class 1 instalment.
Parent's name (mother / father)
Pooja Sachin Jadhav
Usually the mother, because the money goes to the joint account of the girl and her mother.
Parent's Aadhaar number and mobile
Attach a copy of this Aadhaar. Messages about the payment come to the mobile.
House 14, Shivaji Chowk, Malegaon BK, Tal. Baramati, Dist. Pune 413115

Number of living children when applying
Count all living children, sons and daughters.
Joint bank account number (girl and mother)
Open a joint account in the names of the girl and her mother. If the mother has died, open it with the father and attach her death certificate.

BKID0009999 / Malegaon BK

Choose first to fifth. Each later instalment needs a fresh form when the girl reaches that stage.
Register the girl's birth at the gram panchayat or municipal office and collect the birth certificate.

Keep ready the yellow or orange ration card (attested copy), an income certificate of up to Rs.1 lakh from the tehsildar, the parents' Aadhaar and the joint account passbook of the girl and her mother.
Go to your anganwadi centre. The sevika fills in the Lek Ladki form with you, ticks the document checklist, uploads it to the portal and gives you the signed receipt. Keep that receipt.

The anganwadi supervisor checks the papers and the CDPO sends the list to the District Programme Officer of the Zilla Parishad, who approves it. If anything is missing you are told in writing within 15 days and get one month (plus 10 days) to complete it; the whole process should finish within two months.
Once approved, Rs.5,000 is credited by DBT to the joint account of the girl and her mother.

Apply again through the anganwadi with the school bonafide certificate when she enters Class 1, Class 6 and Class 11, and at 18 for the Rs.75,000 with her voter ID and a declaration that she is unmarried.
If the family moves to another district, apply for the remaining instalments to the ICDS office of the new district.
Your anganwadi sevika or the taluka CDPO office; 181 (women's helpline)
Namo Shetkari Mahasanman Nidhi Yojana (Namo Shetkari)
Department of Agriculture, Government of Maharashtra (Commissionerate of Agriculture, Pune)

Rs.6,000 a year from the Maharashtra government to every farmer family that receives PM-Kisan, paid in three instalments of Rs.2,000 straight into the bank account. Together with PM-Kisan's Rs.6,000 that makes Rs.12,000 a year. There is no separate Namo form: the state pays everyone who is eligible for the PM-Kisan instalment, so a farmer not yet on PM-Kisan registers on the PM-Kisan portal, and a farmer already on it who is not getting Namo money checks the status on nsmny.mahait.org and fixes the fault shown. An increase was announced in 2025, so check the portal for the rate in force.
Rs.6,000 a year (3 x Rs.2,000), on top of PM-Kisan's Rs.6,000
Farmer family in Maharashtra that is registered and found eligible under PM-Kisan; whoever qualifies for a PM-Kisan instalment gets the Namo instalment too
Cultivable land in the farmer's own name on the 7/12 extract, with the land seeded on the PM-Kisan record
PM-Kisan e-KYC done, and an Aadhaar-seeded bank account switched on for DBT
Farmer ID (Agristack) is needed for a new PM-Kisan registration

Same exclusions as PM-Kisan: income-tax payers, serving or retired government employees (Class IV staff excepted), pensioners getting Rs.10,000 or more a month, practising doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs and architects, and holders of constitutional posts
7/12 extract and 8A of the land in your name
Mutation entry (ferfar), if the land came to you by inheritance

Farmer ID (Agristack number), made free at a CSC or through the talathi or krushi sahayak
Choose Rural Farmer if your land is in a village; Urban Farmer only if it lies within municipal limits.
Your own 12-digit Aadhaar. It is checked with UIDAI before the form opens.
Best if it is the number linked to your Aadhaar, because the OTP and later e-KYC use it.
Maharashtra
The state where your land is. The portal then checks whether your Farmer ID exists; if not, it offers the steps to make one.
Farmer ID (Agristack)
Get it made first at a CSC or through the talathi with Aadhaar and 7/12. Without it the registration does not go through.
Sanjay Maruti Pawar
Exactly as on Aadhaar. If the 7/12 spells it differently, get one of them corrected, or the land check fails.
Jalna / Ambad / Wadigodri
The village where the land is, as written on the 7/12.

Gat No. 212/2, 1.20 hectares
Copy both from your 7/12 extract. Add every piece of land you hold in your own name.
An account in your own name that is seeded with Aadhaar at the bank. Both PM-Kisan and Namo money come here.
The 11 characters printed on the first page of the passbook.

If you already receive PM-Kisan, do not apply again. Open nsmny.mahait.org and use Beneficiary Status to see your Namo instalments; if one failed, the error-code table on the same page says what to do, such as re-seeding Aadhaar at the bank.
If you are not on PM-Kisan, first get your Farmer ID (Agristack) made at a CSC (Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra) or through the talathi or krushi sahayak, taking Aadhaar and the 7/12.
Open the PM-Kisan New Farmer Registration form, choose Rural Farmer, enter Aadhaar, mobile and the state Maharashtra, and verify with the OTP.
Fill in your name, address, land details from the 7/12 and bank details, upload the 7/12, submit, and note the registration number shown.
The talathi and the taluka agriculture office check the land record, and the state approves it. Finish e-KYC on the portal by OTP or by face authentication.
Once you are approved for PM-Kisan, the Namo instalments follow automatically: Rs.2,000 three times a year, usually soon after each PM-Kisan instalment.
If payments stop, check the status on both portals. The usual causes are pending e-KYC, Aadhaar not seeded with the bank, or land not seeded; the taluka agriculture office can fix the last one.
020-25538755 (Namo Shetkari cell, Commissionerate of Agriculture, Pune); 155261 / 1800-115-526 (PM-Kisan helpline)
Maharashtra Construction Worker Registration (Bandhkam Kamgar Card, MAHABOCW)
Maharashtra Building and Other Construction Workers Welfare Board, Industries, Energy, Labour and Mining Department

You apply online on the board's portal, pick a date, and go once to your taluka construction workers' facilitation centre with the original papers for photo and fingerprint. The registration lasts one year and has to be renewed.
